Definitions.Core.why: the protocol's definitions are trusted text: they import no assumption, guarantee or proof; the accelerator model (Definitions.Core.Accel) is a card's table of numbers and the ACCEL ops, on the tensor-core classes (Definitions.Core.TC.Spec), and the table gives the device model's limits (Card.toDevice), which is trusted text that imports only Mathlib; the server-time blocks and their wipes (Definitions.Core.Blocks) sit on the device model, which is trusted text that imports only Mathlib

Definitions.Core.TC.Pipeline.why: the pipeline parameters both transcriptions read import nothing

Definitions.Core.TC.Spec.why: the semantics (total.py, models.py, term.py) import no proofs and nothing of the relation

Definitions.Core.TC.Relation.why: the relation (relation.py) imports no proofs and nothing of the semantics: the two transcriptions are independent

Definitions.Core.Assumptions.why: a named assumption reads the protocol's definitions, never a guarantee or a proof

Definitions.Core.Guarantees.why: a guarantee is stated over the protocol's definitions with named assumptions as hypotheses, never over a proof

Definitions.Nci.why: the policy is stated over core's model and imports no proofs

Definitions.Nci.Assumptions.why: a named assumption reads the protocol, never a proof

Definitions.Nci.Guarantees.why: a guarantee is a Prop over the protocol and the assumptions, never a proof

Definitions.Pouw.Assumptions.why: a named assumption, and a definition or statement over named assumptions, reads the protocol's definitions, never a guarantee or a proof; the service premises per prover read the claims' collision finders and ecr/sha-512 (Claims.Finder, Claims.ExpectedCR), as C-Flock's guarantees do; the lead's commitment premises read the hash area's keyed leaf and hm96 leaf (Definitions.Hash.Keyed, Definitions.Hash.Hm96)

Definitions.Pouw.Guarantees.why: a guarantee is stated over the protocol's definitions with named assumptions as hypotheses, never over a proof

Definitions.Pouw.Basic.why: probability, integer matrices and oracle programs

Definitions.Pouw.PearlC.Defs.why: Pearl-C's Π, definitions only, over Fp8Atom's definitions: the game and the named assumption read it

Definitions.Accounting.why: resource accounting's definitions are trusted text: the device model, a joint audit's run and the bandwidth and rate audits' games read PoUW's and PoUS's uniform probability and, for the compute audit's embedding, PoUW's game and Pearl-C's; the tensor-core sketch reads the sm_120 E4M3 step's definitions (Definitions.Pouw.Fp8Atom, Definitions.Pouw.PearlC.Sm120); lemma M reads PoUS's audit model (Definitions.Pous.Model.Audit, Definitions.Pous.Model.SampledAudit); the actual circuit is core's circuit placed in space and time (Definitions.Core.Circuit), its runtime's region a declaration (Definitions.Core.Declaration); the actual circuit is core's circuit placed in space and time (Definitions.Core.Circuit), its runtime's region a declaration (Definitions.Core.Declaration), its provers' cost model PoUW's (Definitions.Pouw.Game); B2's responder and lemma M's vocabulary read PoUS's audit game (Definitions.Pous); they import no assumption, guarantee or proof; the bandwidth audit's game reads PoUS's uniform probability under its own layer (Definitions.Accounting.Bandwidth); the remote audit's receipts are the served row leaf in frame-v3-sha512 trees, and their binding event is a collision among the two openings' checks (Definitions.Hash); a period of the causal game reads its subprotocols' collision finders and their success (Definitions.Claims' Finder, Finder.Pr), as the claims state them

Definitions.Accounting.Guarantees.why: the runtime corollary divides the developer's region as NCI does (Definitions.Core.Partition, Definitions.Nci) and takes NCI's named incompressibility assumptions (Definitions.Nci.Assumptions) as hypotheses; B1 is TT at the cost model of the actual circuit's provers; B2 and lemma M compose with PoUS's audit game (Definitions.Pous) and take P2's named assumption P2RingAuditSecure (Definitions.Pous.Assumptions.P2) as a hypothesis; a guarantee is stated over resource accounting's definitions and the device model, with the per-resource guarantees and the named assumptions (PoUW's TT, resource accounting's own) as hypotheses, never over a proof; lemma M's P2 forms read P2's cost model (Definitions.Pous.P2.Cost) and its named assumption (Definitions.Pous.Assumptions.P2); the composed credit's binding lemma (Compose.BindingOfECR) prices a fork by the claims' expected-cost collision resistance (Definitions.Claims' ExpectedCR, Finder), as the claims state it

Definitions.Accounting.Bandwidth.why: the bandwidth audit's game is trusted text: it reads only PoUS's bit strings and uniform probability, and imports no assumption, guarantee or proof; the chip's ports on a strategy's runs (Definitions.Accounting.Bandwidth.Causal) read the actual-circuit model's runs, links and ports (Definitions.Accounting.Confidence)

Definitions.Accounting.Guarantees.Bandwi.why: a guarantee is stated over the bandwidth audit's game, never over a proof

Definitions.Accounting.Assumptions.why: a named assumption of resource accounting (the remote audit's W at the rebuild pricing, Identity, PoUW's conjecture for the bound z) is a Prop over its definitions, never over a guarantee or a proof

Definitions.Claims.why: the claims and the definitions they read are trusted text: they import no assumption, guarantee or proof; messages and collisions are the hash area's (Definitions.Hash.Basic), and Flock's block circuit is core's Boolean circuit (Definitions.Core.Boolean); the interaction model they are stated in, with its messages and collisions, is core's (Definitions.Core.Interaction)

Definitions.Hash.why: the hash area's definitions are trusted text: the served row leaf's formats (frame-v3 trees, sha512/row-seg/v1 and sha512/row/v2, hm96-sha512/v1) over a hash, on Mathlib, core's digests (Definitions.Core.Digest) and core's messages, collisions and byte encodings (Definitions.Core.Hash); they import no assumption, guarantee or proof

Definitions.Hash.Guarantees.why: a guarantee is stated over the hash area's definitions, never over a proof

Definitions.Population.why: populations' definitions are trusted text: they import no assumption, guarantee or proof; a partition of a core circuit is a population

Definitions.Nci.Guarantees.FitRate.why: the fit bound on a run is stated over NCI's window premises and the actual circuit's windows (Definitions.Accounting), never over a proof

Definitions.Flock.why: C-Flock's definitions, extracted from Proofs/Flock, are trusted text: they import no assumption, guarantee or proof; the audit partitions core's Boolean circuit (Definitions.Core.Boolean); a Merkle collision is the hash area's (Definitions.Hash.Basic); the game's uniform average and probability, and the draw law, are core's (Definitions.Core.Game, Definitions.Core.Draw)

Definitions.Accounting.JointBridge.CommO.why: the network certifier's bridge to the joint period reads the period run (Definitions.Accounting.JointPeriod), the network certifier's window good event (Definitions.NetworkCertifier.Period), and the deployed network certifier's code and record format (Definitions.NetworkCertifier.Tap) with its trust, trusted-host (Definitions.Core.Assumptions), which the run carries as a field; it imports no guarantee or proof

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingAuditSecure.why: P2 in the ring model at the deployed point accepts a rho-bounded, (D, Q, L)-bounded responder with probability at most 1% + 2^-129 + 2^-130; open, and, if p is prime, false at D >= 32,894 (Q >= 2, L >= 65,789) for every k (PousP2Ring.tight_p16448, Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RingTight.lean), and at L >= 2^30 for k <= 88 (PousP2Ring.not_meetsOn_b19_k88, Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RingTrunc.lean); and, at k = 105, from L >= 2^169 with D >= 2 and Q >= 2 (Pous.Period.SecurityProofs.not_p2RingAuditSecure_trunc, Security/Proofs/Pous/PeriodDeployed.lean: 501,819 blocks without their low 168 bits), so the deployed budget (16,446, 2^20, 2^64) lies outside every refuted region. Its test plays the ring-model audit at a scaled point (w = 184, 16 blocks, lambda = 9) with those two attacks and seeded bounded responders.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingReducesToM1p.why: Every ring-model responder against P2 at k = 105 is matched up to 2^-130 by an m1p responder with 128 more bits per block (P2-M1-SGI); open, and it implies P2RingAuditSecure, so a refutation of that is one of this.

Pouw.Fp8Atom.H1T.DistinctLiveH1T.why: On every legal unit, H-1T's credited words are pairwise distinct functions of the unit's salt and none is free; open, with no counterexample on the legal units its test enumerates or samples.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingRoundSecure.why: P2 in the ring model per round, at every block count from 2^19 to 2^25: at a boundary held at most rho*|C| bits, outside an event of mass k*eps0 over k rounds, a uniform challenge is answered with probability at most 1 - p given the earlier answers; open, and, if p is prime, it forces p = 0 at D >= 32,894 (Q >= 2, L >= 65,789) whenever eps0 < 1 and m/N <= 1 - p + eps0 at L >= 2^(t+1) for m blocks kept without t low bits (p = 0.043 false from L >= 2^167 at 2^19 when eps0 <= 2^-130), which Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RoundTests.lean proves.

Accounting.Assumptions.EncodeChainHardne.why: In the circuit model, computing q distinct words of the masked k-round codec's encoding, less parity, on more than ε of the draws costs q·E budgeted units less E/(n−1) per run-input bit, inside the floor its statement carries (ε ≥ 2^−64, k ≥ 1, p ≥ 2^66, p ≡ 3 mod 4); false at every E ≥ 1 and every B inside that floor (26 Oct 2026, Accounting.SecurityProofs.Gates.EncodeChainRefuted, note:20261026T0110Z-report-s5-lowerbounds): an AND of two bits is a free s8-family MAC and NOT a free affine map, so a restricted circuit with no budgeted gate and no run input computes any number of words for the key's gather units (bitwise_codec.py, 8 units a key byte). The model now charges every product of two data values a unit (Gates.nonlinear), and SquaringFloor and ChainSum replace it; it stays listed so that anything citing it shows up.

Accounting.Assumptions.TS.LinSteer.why: SAMPLING's LIN-STEER, that zeroing a fraction phi of a row's noise-active coordinates saves at most phi of the consumer's work; false for every segmented consumer whose noise-active segments carry unequal counts (Accounting.SecurityProofs.TS.LinSteerSegments, LinSteerFalse).

Nci.Assumptions.ActivationsSupport.why: ActivationsIncompressible in support form; false at FP4 for every chain, updated or not (19 Oct 2026, note:compute-accounting/20261019T0725Z-finding-nci-falsify, art:d2cc129951081405e9b3f465d03ecc6f2760ce4dec82768125fce5b8052c4c32): T one first-multiplication product gate holding an E2M1 x E2M1 product is charged b_w + b_a and takes at most 37 values, so it fails at every cap >= b_w + b_a once b_w + b_a > log2 37 = 5.21 (the calculator's 2.5 + 4 = 6.5). Nci.SecurityProofs.IuReads rests on it, and so do Nci.SecurityProofs.ContainedMatMul and ContainedTraining.

Accounting.Assumptions.TS.FoldOptFoldedA.why: FOLD-OPT per word folded at the one certificate a headline prices at: at pi*, no run folds its words at a price below (1 - mu_f)·folded·phi*(pi*). Open; at every certificate (FoldOptFolded) it is false: the IMAD rotate, a bit-exact fold of LOP3 and four IMAD-pipe instructions a word, costs 14 to the menu's 16 halfway between DS-120's issue and LOP rows (RT2-LOGIC-1). Its test prices each bit-exact fold we know (the menu's, the funnel, shift, IMAD and wide rotates, the wide multiplies) at both sm_120 headlines' pi* against phi*. On the B200's two readings it is false at every certificate too (RT3-LOGIC-6: ♭'s fold with each IMAD as 32 ALU shift-adds); on the H200's three (DC-90-ri's at 1/2 and its (I3) twin at 3/5 among them) that fold breaks it at no certificate, since the H200's menu holds each route with LI's multiplies as IMAD.WIDE and N_w times one of those prices at most that fold on every row. benchmarks/pouw/tests/test_lean_headline_dc.py::test_folds_meet_fold_opt_at_pi_star prices ♭'s fold and that one at each of the five pi* and checks both facts. At those pi* it is open on all five, and every class a fold route issues prices above 0 at each (a free class would make it harder to meet, not easier: HB-PROOF's M1). On the H200 the cheater's menu holds every counted fold known to come near the bit-exact loops, none built: RT4-SHEET-13's and -14's moves of LI on li and each loop (its XORs as a memory round trip of three issue slots, its multiplies as IMAD.WIDE, or both), their classes at the JI90 lines the H200 measured beside the IGMMA (r20261021-070616-d06c, r20261021-074303-da7f, r20261021-161119-62ac), and li-bulk at its measured cost (r20261021-161119-62ac) with its counted BT1024 and trimmed infinite-W members (RT4-SHEET-17, -22), so there it is a premise only about folds off the cheater's menu, and a counted fold priced below what it would cost built only lowers the proved credit (1 - epsilon)·B_flat, which reads w* and phi* at pi* and not B_flat (RT4-SHEET-27); B_flat doesn't move with it, since flat folds by the built routes alone. The two-slot round trip is off the menu: li's XOR has three inputs a half step and one ATOM.E.XOR and one LD.E carry two. At the (I3) twin's pi* it doesn't follow from FOLD-OPT at 1/2's (HB-PROOF's M1), and phi* there is li-bulk's trimmed member.

Nci.Assumptions.PartialSumsSupport.why: PartialSumsIncompressible in support form; false for one honest matrix multiplication with binary additions, inside the caps (19 Oct 2026, note:compute-accounting/20261019T0725Z-finding-nci-falsify, art:d2cc129951081405e9b3f465d03ecc6f2760ce4dec82768125fce5b8052c4c32): with product IUs that fix a column over a block of (i, t) and adder IUs over k x k x k blocks, each entry's products lie in d IUs while each IU's support is bounded by the entries it depends on; the exact 1-bit toy (d = e = N = 8, b_w = b_a = 1) can be charged at most 183 against the 448 required, for every Gamma >= 448 and K >= 512, and at d = 7168, K = 2e7 the division absorbs at most 8.4% (FP4) and 17.8% (FP8) of the charge at (2.5, 4). Nci.SecurityProofs.ContainedMatMul and ContainedTraining rest on it.

Nci.Assumptions.ReferenceLayered.why: The reference training circuit, written in the declarations' Dot16 steps, has a threading with a keyed form (Layered) at Kimi K2's shapes: roots of at least 17 legs (the previous accumulator and 16 activations), at most 2,328 counted Dot16 steps (37,248 products) reaching any one value, none reaching a lookup (layer 0's attention-input projections uncounted), and bf16 embedding columns of 163,840 x 16 bits; open, checked against a transformer block on paper only (the Notion page "Threading at Dot16 granularity", https://app.notion.com/p/3fe399515d9e81108139f66cfd33db94), since no Lean reference circuit of a transformer exists to build one on. Its test checks that these are Kimi K2's shapes' parameters (kappa.py) in the steps of the declared BF16 GEMM (GEMM_HOPPER's HopperBF16WgmmaDot16, 16 activations a step, verity/ml/circuits/ops/boolean/gemm.py), at capacity factor 1 and with bf16 embeddings, neither of which any workload declares, and that tiers.py's (d, e) = (10, 37248) is what ReferenceThreaded derives from them at S = K (E = 7 columns, e in products); it cannot find a reference circuit that is not keyed.

Nci.Assumptions.WeightsSupport.why: WeightsIncompressible in support form; false at FP4 at b_a = 4 under the standard threading (19 Oct 2026, Linear CMP-56, note:compute-accounting/20261019T0725Z-finding-nci-falsify, art:32d42058ab76d8012ef741449665e9e1c2a444fa7158bcb03cbf2457b97944dd): with each FP4 thread value a gate holding its E2M1 value (15 values), one wgrad product delta_t[i] * x_t[j] reads 2 thread values and no weight, charged 8 against support <= 225 < 2^8, and 16 fprop products sharing one weight are charged 66.5 against <= 2^66.42; with E2M1 codes (16 with -0) and each block scale in its own gate, an NVFP4 or MXFP4 block of codes always holds a code of magnitude >= 3, so 16 wgrad products over one 16-token block are charged 128 against <= 2^127.998. It holds against these at FP8 (E4M3, 7.98 bits per entry) and when each FP4 gate holds its scaled value. Nci.SecurityProofs.ThreadedReadsInfo, ThreadedContainedInfo and ThreadedOfState rest on it.

Nci.Assumptions.Reach.why: Reach is a predicate on the threading T (FitBoundSlots for ReachSlots, Reach counted in parameter slots). fit.py's rungs use it at token threads (reuse 2), where ASK-68 (19 Oct) adopts it for dense recipes, each of whose tokens uses all its weights; there it is false for a token-routed MoE, Kimi K2 (about 32B active) and GLM-5.3 (about 40B) being under N* = 87.6B. At sequence threads it is the per-sequence form, whose reuse cost is the T.reuse already in FitBound, twice the sequence length, which voids the rungs. Open over all recipes (LEAN-35, F1); its test checks that N* is at most the weights one sequence reaches under kappa.py's MoE routing at Kimi K2's shapes, and more than one token reaches.

Nci.Assumptions.ReachSlots.why: Reach is a predicate on the threading T (FitBoundSlots for ReachSlots, Reach counted in parameter slots). fit.py's rungs use it at token threads (reuse 2), where ASK-68 (19 Oct) adopts it for dense recipes, each of whose tokens uses all its weights; there it is false for a token-routed MoE, Kimi K2 (about 32B active) and GLM-5.3 (about 40B) being under N* = 87.6B. At sequence threads it is the per-sequence form, whose reuse cost is the T.reuse already in FitBound, twice the sequence length, which voids the rungs. Open over all recipes (LEAN-35, F1); its test checks that N* is at most the weights one sequence reaches under kappa.py's MoE routing at Kimi K2's shapes, and more than one token reaches.

Nci.Assumptions.WeightsSupportFmt.why: WeightsSupport with each thread charged by its work at log2 n - mu; false at the deployed point (d = 2048, e = 4e4, E4M3 at rate 4, S = 2e7, b_w = 2.5) on its weight term and its margin (19 Oct 2026, NCI-FALSIFY, note:compute-accounting/20261019T0725Z-finding-nci-falsify, art:11fe95233ee17d4b013ddb1699b39f8e9656adc48ae17909efa46bc4ecbcccf2): one AdamW step after the checkpoint a weight lies in an interval theta fixes, so one token's 16,384 fprop products on a DeepSeek-V3 128 x 128 E4M3 block are charged 40,961.6 bits against <= 29,113 (false for b_w > 1.78 at sigma 0.006, over the first 1, 3 and 7 steps at sigma 0.006, 0.01 and 0.02); an NVFP4 16 x 16 2D-block weight quantized for fprop and again for dgrad is two weight gates, charged 1,280 against <= 1,269 (false for every b_w > 2.153); llama-3-405b's gate+up fan-out 106,496 exceeds e log2 n / rate, and its FP8 run is charged 2.077e7 against <= 1.947e7. Nci.SecurityProofs.ThreadedReadsInfoFmt, ThreadedContainedInfoFmt and ThreadedOfStateFmt rest on it; WeightsSupportFmt2 restates it.

Accounting.Assumptions.SquaringFloor.why: In the circuit model's nonlinear units (Definitions/Accounting/Gates: window proven by interval analysis; the only free operations are linear maps with coefficients fixed before the coins, so a cost is the budgeted units and a unit per data product, an s8-family lane whose two multiplicands both depend on run or coin data, whatever their range), one squaring mod p from a word's canonical bytes to n/8 byte-format limbs congruent to its square, right on more than ε of the words, costs at least e nonlinear units, at ε ≥ 2^−64 and p ≥ 2^66; open, priced e = (2L − 1) + (L − d(ε)), d(ε) = 4 + ⌈log₂(1/ε)/8⌉ (374 at p1024 and ε = 2^−40): the 2L − 1 column sums' multiplicative complexity (sketched) plus the red team's Lemma R at c = 0. Every known construction sits above it (ripple carries 16,896, 3-limb look-ahead 16,726). Its test builds them and checks each costs at least e, its column sums L² data products.

Accounting.Assumptions.ChainSum.why: In the circuit model's nonlinear units, if one squaring mod p costs e nonlinear units (SquaringFloor), the masked k-round codec's words cost k·S·e nonlinear units each (S = Field.squarings, 1,021 at p1024), less a word per n − 1 run-input bits (Gates.EncodeBound at E = k·S·e), at ε ≥ 2^−64, k ≥ 1, p ≥ 2^66 and p ≡ 3 mod 4: Sloth's sequentiality (Lenstra–Wesolowski) in the model, the roots' squarings in sequence and no work shared across words; open. Its test chains the known squarings at p1024 and checks the chain costs their sum, and the bitwise codec's data products are measured in benchmarks/property_redteam/tests/test_bitwise_codec.py.

Pous.P2.Assumptions.P2RingRoundSecureWid.why: P2RingRoundSecure's statement at every block count from 2^19 to 2^27, so that it reaches the demo's 1038*2^16 blocks; open and unchecked in N above 2^25 (the eps0 a proof would give against N is pending the memory-accounting lane's pous-chain analysis); it implies P2RingRoundSecure (Pous.SecurityProofs.roundSecure_of_wide), so every refutation of that one (PousP2Rounds.round_tight and round_trunc, Security/Proofs/Pous/P2/RoundTests.lean) refutes it, and its falsification test is that one's, whose scaled point doesn't depend on N.
